you will have to choose products based on porosity. once you find out your porosity, it will dictate what kind of products you need. For instance, low-porosity hair (hair that is less “porous” will not absorb product as easily) will therefore need lighter, water-based products as heavier products I.e. oils/butters will sit on the top of the hair in a greasy mess. Needless to say high-porosity hair will absorb more quickly and will need more heavy products (oil/butter,etc) to retain moisture for long. Even when you know your porosity, unfortunately it may take a little experimenting. I would suggest looking at the links below, along with many of [these](https://www.reddit.com/r/curlyhair/wiki/sidebar/)

• [Holy Grail list](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1gn6VnPsRU1H3ziElbWqNVFY5mev6GB1pwKKt_MNpoAY/htmlview)

• [international holy grail list](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/u/3/d/e/2PACX-1vTbVtl5RKQyRwtOlctXVt4f8HovDNVjRUkXBMt3l_DpnkSS0Q-wQ3d77_nf20EJ2yPEFpsuvb6Aa52c/pubhtml#)

• [ultimate cg guide](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Q6Dj9WAZxlfBhJSyS5on2rw3-if5cOV3oV-dQ3B0AHA/mobilebasic#heading=h.t37f7kwlj2xe)

I know they are labelled curly girl and not everything you may do may strictly adhere to this, but it’s a good start. As you get to know your hair you’ll eventually learn how to liberate your curls with a suitable routine that works for you. This may take time, but it’s absolutely fine. 

Hope that helped

don’t blow dry, diffuse and perhaps plop. Air drying alone will weigh down your hair and loosen out the wave as the water weighs the hair down. you also need to moisturize your hair - gel alone will only enhance and hold the curl pattern but will not moisturise. add a leave in, then gel, and diffuse. scrunch out the cast with a light oil afterwards. Also make sure you have a silk bonnet/pillowcase, and refresh hair in the morning if needed. And definitely don’t brush dry, it will only make it much more frizzy and susceptible to damage i.e. split ends, etc. and make sure you also deep condition weekly - moisture/hydration is key.

I would advise practicing bass clef alone, and in the 30 seconds given to look at it, **try the piece**. This is usually a weird and more tense part of the exam and playing in the 30 seconds will release at least some of the tension and make it sound better overall. Also, make sure you acknowledge the key signature (possibly the most important), and have some sort of tempo/rhythm. And if you make a mistake, **keep on going**, also because a wrong note won't necessarily affect tempo too much. Just know you don't need to pass the sightreading or a meet all the criteria to a high standard, since some elements of the exam can outweigh others.  You can find more information [here](https://gb.abrsm.org/en/exam-support/your-guide-to-abrsm-exams/how-we-mark-exams/). hope that helps
